football_evidence.question: Can Wisconsin take away UCLA’s big plays?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward UCLA, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.0 of the 2.9 points, but not the full gap. Input warning: EdgeDesk’s published number sits 6.7 points from the middle of its own other models. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When UCLA has the ball (big plays on the ground): UCLA’s offense turns 11.8% of its runs into explosive gains, and Wisconsin’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.6% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When UCLA has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): UCLA’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 8.1% of its runs, and Wisconsin’s defense stops 11.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Wisconsin has the ball (big plays on the ground): Wisconsin’s offense turns 5.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and UCLA’s defense gives up explosive gains on 1.7% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
When UCLA has the ball (the run game against the run defense): UCLA’s offense averages 7.1 yards per carry, and Wisconsin’s defense allows 3.6 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).
contradicting: When Wisconsin has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Wisconsin’s offense has allowed a sack on 2.1% of its dropbacks, and UCLA’s defense sacks the quarterback on 4.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When UCLA has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): UCLA’s offense averages 7.9 yards per pass attempt, and Wisconsin’s defense allows 4.7 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.5).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Wisconsin’s linebackers No. 46 nationally and UCLA’s No. 81.

When Wisconsin has the ball (big plays through the air): Wisconsin’s offense turns 12.0% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and UCLA’s defense gives up explosive gains on 10.7% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).
quarterbacks: Nico Iamaleava has completed 61 of 99 passes (61.6%) for 816 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in four games for UCLA, and has been sacked on 6 of 105 dropbacks.
Colton Joseph has completed 80 of 142 passes (56.3%) for 1,132 yards, 8.0 yards per attempt, 9 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in five games for Wisconsin, and has been sacked on 3 of 145 dropbacks.
